projects.title: AI Resume Analyzer
projects.summary: LLM-powered resume screening tool that scores a CV against a job description and returns structured, explainable feedback.
projects.description: An applicant-tracking-friendly analyzer that parses resumes, extracts structured entities, embeds both the resume and the job description, and produces a match score with concrete improvement suggestions.
features: PDF and DOCX parsing with layout-aware text extraction
Semantic match scoring against any job description
Skill gap detection with rewrite suggestions
projects.problem: Candidates rarely know why a resume is filtered out, and small teams cannot manually review hundreds of applications per role.
projects.solution: Combine deterministic parsing with embedding-based similarity and an LLM reasoning layer that explains the score instead of only producing a number.
projects.architecture: React client → FastAPI service → parser + embedding pipeline → vector store for JD/resume chunks → LLM scoring chain → cached JSON report.
challenges: Controlling token cost on long documents
results: Screening time per resume reduced from minutes to seconds
Structured JSON output usable directly by an ATS
projects.lessons: Retrieval quality matters more than prompt cleverness; strict output schemas make LLM features shippable.

projects.title: Banking Data Analytics Dashboard
projects.summary: Transaction analytics dashboard surfacing success rates, failure categories and SLA breaches across digital banking journeys.
projects.description: A reporting layer built on PostgreSQL that aggregates transaction events into daily, channel-wise and failure-reason views for operations and business stakeholders.
features: Channel-wise transaction success and failure trends
Failure reason drilldowns with root cause tagging
Automated daily refresh via Python jobs
SLA breach alerting with threshold configuration
projects.problem: Operations teams relied on manual spreadsheets to understand daily transaction failures, which delayed incident response.
projects.solution: Model the raw event data into analytical views, automate the refresh, and give stakeholders a single dashboard with drilldowns.
projects.architecture: Transaction tables → SQL aggregation views → Python ETL job → reporting schema → Power BI dashboards.
challenges: Query performance over very large partitions
results: Report preparation time cut from hours to minutes
5x faster reporting queries after index and CTE rework
Single source of truth for failure categorisation
projects.lessons: Agreeing on metric definitions is harder — and more valuable — than building the dashboard.

projects.title: Customer Churn Prediction
projects.summary: End-to-end churn model with feature engineering, class-imbalance handling and business-facing risk segments.
projects.description: A supervised classification pipeline that predicts customer churn probability and converts it into actionable retention segments.
projects.problem: Retention campaigns were sent to everyone, wasting budget on customers who were never going to leave.
projects.solution: Train and evaluate several classifiers, then expose calibrated probabilities as three actionable risk tiers.
projects.architecture: Raw customer data → cleaning + feature store → train/validate split → model comparison → calibrated model → scored segments export.
results: Clear feature-importance narrative for the business
projects.lessons: A slightly worse model that stakeholders trust beats a better model nobody uses.

projects.title: Fraud Detection using ML
projects.summary: Anomaly detection service that flags suspicious transactions in near real time with tunable precision.
projects.description: Hybrid rules plus model scoring service designed for a high-volume payments stream where false positives are expensive.
features: Rule engine plus ML score blending
projects.problem: Static rules missed novel fraud patterns and produced too many false alerts.
projects.solution: Blend a supervised score with deterministic rules and let analysts tune the operating point.
projects.architecture: Transaction stream → feature enrichment → model scoring API → rule blending → alert queue with feedback capture.
results: False positive rate reduced meaningfully at equal recall
Retraining loop driven by analyst labels
projects.lessons: In fraud, the operating point is a business decision, not a modelling one.

projects.title: E-commerce Data Pipeline
projects.summary: Batch ETL pipeline consolidating orders, inventory and marketing data into an analytics-ready warehouse schema.
projects.description: An idempotent, incrementally-loading pipeline with validation gates and clear failure semantics.
projects.problem: Business metrics were computed inconsistently from three disconnected source systems.
projects.solution: Land, clean and conform the sources into one warehouse schema with tested transformations.
projects.architecture: Sources → landing zone → cleaning layer → conformed dimensions and facts → reporting views.
results: Failures isolated to a single stage
projects.lessons: Idempotency is what makes an ETL pipeline operable at 3am.

projects.architecture: Producer → Kafka topic → streaming consumer with windowed state → metrics store → live dashboard endpoint.

projects.title: Portfolio Website

projects.summary: Offline-first notes application with markdown editing, tagging and instant fuzzy search.
projects.description: A small, fast note-taking app built around local-first storage with background sync.

blogs.title: SQL Performance Lessons From a Banking Platform
blogs.excerpt: What actually made our reporting queries 5x faster — and the optimisations that turned out to be noise.
blogs.content:
## The setup

Reporting queries over a high-volume transaction table were taking minutes. The dataset was partitioned, indexed and, on paper, fine.

## What actually helped

1. **Reading the execution plan first.** Most guesses were wrong. The plan was not.
2. **Replacing correlated subqueries with window functions.** One rewrite removed a nested loop over millions of rows.
3. **Composite indexes ordered by selectivity.** Column order matters more than column count.
4. **Materialising the aggregation layer.** Not every query needs to be live.

```sql
SELECT channel,
       date_trunc('day', created_at) AS day,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'SUCCESS') AS success,
       count(*) AS total
FROM transactions
WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY 1, 2;
```

## What did not help

Adding indexes speculatively, rewriting joins into CTEs for readability alone, and increasing work_mem without measuring.

## Takeaway

Measure, change one thing, measure again. Performance work without a baseline is just refactoring.

blogs.title: Shipping LLM Features That Do Not Break in Production
blogs.excerpt: Strict schemas, retrieval quality and cost guardrails matter far more than prompt wording.
blogs.content:
## The uncomfortable truth

Most LLM demos fail in production for boring reasons: unpredictable output shape, runaway cost and irrelevant retrieval.

## Three rules I follow

### 1. Enforce a schema

Validate every response against a schema and retry on failure. Free-form text is not an API.

```python
class Score(BaseModel):
    match: int
    gaps: list[str]
    summary: str
```

### 2. Fix retrieval before prompts

If the right chunk never reaches the model, no prompt saves you. Chunking strategy is the feature.

### 3. Budget tokens explicitly

Cap input length, cache aggressively and log cost per request from day one.

## Takeaway

Treat the model as an unreliable service you wrap carefully — not as magic.

blogs.title: Python Automation That Pays For Itself in a Week
blogs.excerpt: How to pick which manual task to automate first, and how to make the script survive contact with reality.
blogs.content:
## Pick the right target

Automate the task that is frequent, deterministic and painful — in that order. A weekly two-hour task beats a rare four-hour one.

## Make it boring

- Idempotent runs
- Explicit logging
- Fail loudly, never silently
- Configuration outside the code

```python
def run(config: Config) -> Report:
    rows = fetch(config)
    issues = validate(rows)
    notify(issues)
    return Report(len(rows), len(issues))
```

## Measure the saving

Record the manual baseline before you start. It is the only way to prove the value later.

## Takeaway

Automation is a product with one user. Treat that user well.

blogs.title: From MERN to Data: What Transferred and What Did Not
blogs.excerpt: Moving from full stack product work into banking data analytics changed how I think about correctness.
blogs.content:
## What transferred

API thinking, debugging instinct, version control discipline and the habit of writing things down.

## What did not

In product work, a bug is annoying. In banking data, an incorrect number is a compliance event. The bar for verification is completely different.

## The bridge skill

SQL. It is the one language that stays useful whether you are building a dashboard, an API or a model.

## Takeaway

Breadth is only valuable if each area is deep enough to be trusted.
